rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the maximum annual rent increase is 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Multiply base rent by .016 to get the maximum dollar increase.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the current annual-increase period; the percentage is reset each March 1. The underlying ordinance predates this period.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units; units with a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979 and Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies are exempt from the increase limits.
rules.exemptions: Post-June 13, 1979 CO units, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated tenancies.
rules.interaction: Local rent control governs; the state cap in Civ. Code § 1947.12 exempts housing under stricter local rent control.
rules.conflict_note: Coverage of the Costa-Hawkins and other exemptions cannot be verified from parcel data. The 1979 CO cutoff comes from D079.

unverifiable_exemptions: Costa-Hawkins exemptions (single-family homes, condos, tenancies that began after the prior tenant left)
tenancies regulated by other government agencies

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance just cause eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of 17 listed just causes, and the just cause must be the dominant motive. Expiration of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and removing housing services such as parking or storage also needs just cause.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes; dominant motive required
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not give an effective date.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance. Includes some units exempt from the rent increase limits (post-June 13, 1979 CO units, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated tenancies).
rules.penalty: Unlawful evictions or attempts may result in substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.interaction: Applies even to tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits; local just cause governs over the state rule.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancies in units regulated by other government agencies
owner-occupancy and other exemptions under the Rent Ordinance

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance relocation payments for no-fault evictions (incl. Ellis Act)
rules.requirement: For no-fault evictions (owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal, temporary capital improvements, substantial rehabilitation), the landlord must pay relocation per tenant, up to a per-unit maximum, plus an extra amount for each elderly, disabled or minor-child household. Ellis Act evictions have a higher schedule. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served.
rules.key_value: Notices served 3/1/2026–2/28/2027: $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor child; Ellis Act: $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13, plus $7,443.90
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the rate period in effect on 2026-10-01. Rates adjust each March 1 and the underlying schedule dates from 2006.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance; amount is fixed by the date the eviction notice is served.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9, not § 37.9C.

unverifiable_exemptions: government-owned or certain subsidized housing exempt under the Rent Ordinance

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords and vendors may not sell or use algorithmic devices (software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data) to recommend rents or manage occupancy for residential units. Tenants or the City Attorney can sue, and each unit-month can be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor rental data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law
rules.effective_date_note: SF.gov (D081) says it went into effect October 14, 2024. Law-firm sources say only 'October 2024'.
rules.penalty: Civil action by a tenant or the City Attorney; damages, injunctive relief, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with each unit-month a separate violation (per D002).

rules.title: SF security deposit interest rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the rate period stated in the document.
rules.conflict_note: The document gives the rate but does not cite the code section. The § 49.2 citation is not stated in the source.

rules.title: SF Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: People with arrest or conviction history are protected in affordable housing decisions. The document does not detail the specific requirements.
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
rules.conflict_note: The document is a landing page and gives no code section or operative detail. Coverage is limited to affordable housing, which parcel data cannot show.

requires_unknown_facts: unit is in an affordable housing project

parsed.notes: Merged duplicate SF § 37.10C records (c68, c78, c91), the allowable-increase records (c67, c70) and the relocation records (c69, c71, c72). The 1979 CO cutoff on the rent cap comes from D079. Just cause carries no cutoff. No SF document covers application-fee rules. The Fair Chance record is low confidence because the source is a landing page.
